notes: Como el usuario dijo explícitamente 'no quiero correr', el modelo base ya capta bien la intención sin necesitar el skill. La diferencia con la versión con skill es más de matiz (el skill evita por completo estructurar la progresión como 'cada vez más trote', el baseline todavía la organiza así aunque cierre con el mensaje correcto) que de resultado observable.
Assertion 'usa los N días disponibles' and 'incluye taper' pass in both configurations on most evals - not very discriminating on their own.
Eval 'weight-loss-knee-injury': without_skill fails 2/5 assertions (no block structure with review checkpoints, no explicit age-52 mention) - with_skill passes all 5.

Eval 'zero-to-30-min': without_skill takes a risky progression jump (12min continuous to 20min continuous in one week, ~67% increase) violating safe progression; with_skill spreads the same milestone gradually over ~24 weeks in 4-week blocks instead of 9. This is the clearest safety-relevant difference found.

Evals 'first-3k-8-weeks' and 'walk-run-only-knee-pain' show no measurable pass-rate difference: the base model already handles these patterns well (well-documented 'couch to 5K'-style progressions, and an explicit 'I don't want to run' instruction that's easy to follow either way).

with_skill runs take roughly 2-3x longer and use ~35% more tokens than without_skill, mainly from reading SKILL.md plus the relevant reference file(s) before answering - reasonable overhead for the quality/safety gains observed, but worth knowing.
